balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

nim.title: Net interest margin and spread
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income as a percentage of interest-earning assets; net interest spread is the lending yield less the funding cost (the two don't move identically because NIM is also diluted by non-earning assets).

For Genertec Universal Medical Group's Finance segment: this is the core profitability metric of the ~RMB70bn finance-leasing/factoring book that originated the company. Spread widened to 3.80-4.42% through FY2025-H1 FY2026 even as rates fell generally, as lower funding costs outpaced yield compression on the hospital-lease book.

What to watch:

  • Spread trend versus NIM -- a widening gap signals a growing non-earning-asset drag
  • Funding cost versus lending yield to hospitals and healthcare-adjacent borrowers

segmentRevenue.title: Finance vs Healthcare segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Genertec Universal Medical Group runs two integrated segments: Finance (leasing, factoring and supply-chain finance, mostly to hospitals) and Healthcare (67 owned/operated hospitals plus healthcare-technology and specialty-medical units).

For this company: Healthcare overtook Finance as the larger segment around FY2021-2022 and was ~66% of FY2025 income; Finance revenue has been roughly flat (RMB4.8-5.9bn/yr since FY2019) while Healthcare has nearly quadrupled over the same period. The mix shift matters because the two segments carry very different capital intensity, growth rates and risk (lender credit risk vs. hospital operating risk).

What to watch:

  • Whether Finance revenue growth re-accelerates or stays a stable, low-growth funding engine for Healthcare's equipment purchases
  • Healthcare revenue growth decelerating as the hospital base matures

niea.title: Net interest-earning assets
niea.content:
The finance-lease and factoring receivables (and related earning assets) that generate the Finance segment's net interest income -- the balance-sheet scale behind the NIM/spread percentages.

For this company: the book grew from ~RMB50bn (FY2019) to ~RMB71bn (FY2024) before dipping slightly in FY2025, then recovering to ~RMB71bn by H1 FY2026 -- a lender whose asset growth has plateaued even as rate spread improved, consistent with a deliberate shift of capital toward the faster-growing Healthcare segment.

What to watch:

  • Book growth (or shrinkage) versus the NIM/spread trend -- margin expansion on a shrinking book is a different story than on a growing one
  • Concentration risk: how much of the book is lent to the Group's own hospitals versus third parties

assetQuality.title: Asset quality: NPL ratio, overdue ratio and provision coverage
assetQuality.content:
NPL ratio is non-performing finance-lease/factoring receivables as a percentage of the book; 30-day overdue ratio is a leading indicator (loans that have started slipping but are not yet classified non-performing); provision coverage is loan-loss allowance as a percentage of NPLs.

For this company: the NPL ratio has held in a tight 0.9-1.0% band since FY2019 -- low for a lender to hospitals, many of which are smaller, non-Group institutions -- while provision coverage has risen steadily from ~238% (FY2021) to ~339% (H1 FY2026), meaning reserves have been built up faster than problem loans, a conservative signal. The 30-day overdue ratio ticking up to 0.95-0.97% in FY2024 and H1 FY2026 versus the NPL ratio is worth watching as an early-warning lead indicator.

What to watch:

  • 30-day overdue ratio rising ahead of the NPL ratio (early warning of future NPL formation)
  • Provision coverage falling while NPL ratio rises (reserve-adequacy warning) -- not the current pattern, but the risk to monitor

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Genertec Universal Medical Group Company Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
